hints: Look at what each test is really asking for, carbonyl group, aldehyde group, and methyl-carbonyl group.
The Fehling's result narrows it down a lot, since only aldehydes (not ketones) give that red-brown precipitate.
Now ask which aldehyde also gives a pale yellow precipitate with alkaline iodine, that points to the one containing a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group.
walkthrough:
**Decode the 2,4-DNPH test**

Great start. An orange precipitate with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine means Q must contain a carbonyl group, $\text{C=O}$.

So Q is either an aldehyde or a ketone. This rules out alcohols straight away.

**Decode the Fehling's test**

This is the key filter. Fehling's reagent is oxidised from blue to a red-brown precipitate of $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ only by aldehydes.

$$\text{RCHO} + 2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 5\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^- + \text{Cu}_2\text{O} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Ketones are not oxidised, so they give no reaction. Q must therefore be an aldehyde.

**Decode the iodoform test**

A pale yellow precipitate with alkaline aqueous iodine is $\text{CHI}_3$, iodoform. This positive result needs a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group or a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}$ group that can be oxidised to it.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 + \text{HCOO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Put all three clues together**

Q must be an aldehyde AND contain the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ unit. Ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, is the only aldehyde in the list that does both.

options.A: Ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$, fits all three. It has $\text{C=O}$ so gives orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. It is an aldehyde so reduces Fehling's to red-brown $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$. It has the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group so gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline iodine.
options.B: Propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, has a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}$ group so it can give a positive iodoform test, but it is an alcohol with no $\text{C=O}$. It will not give an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH and will not react with Fehling's.
options.C: Propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, is an aldehyde so it passes the first two tests, but its structure is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$, not $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$. It therefore gives no yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate. This is the classic trap of forgetting the iodoform requirement.
options.D: Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, is a ketone with a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group so it passes the 2,4-DNPH and iodoform tests, but ketones cannot be oxidised by Fehling's. It gives no red-brown precipitate, so it fails the second test.
